chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from Ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “The woman in nifās remains seated for nineteen nights; then if she sees blood, she acts as the mustaḥāḍah acts.”
And we have also narrated from Ibn Sinān that which conflicts with this report, namely that the days of nifās are like the days of menstruation; thus, the two reports are in conflict.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ ٱلنُّفَسَاءِ: the days assigned to postpartum bleeding
key_terms.تَعَارَضَ ٱلْخَبَرَانِ: the two reports are in conflict
key_terms.تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ لَيْلَةً: nineteen nights, the period mentioned here for nifās
key_terms.دَمًا: blood seen after the stated period
key_terms.ٱلنُّفَسَاءُ: a woman in the state of postpartum bleeding
key_terms.ٱلْحَيْضِ: menstruation, used here as a point of comparison
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, whose legal rulings differ from nifās and ḥayḍ

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the duration of nifās and the conflicting reports about it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling of nifās, stating that a postpartum woman refrains for nineteen nights, and if she continues to see blood thereafter, she follows the ruling of a mustaḥāḍah. The closing note records that another report from Ibn Sinān gives a different ruling, indicating a conflict between the two narrations in legal discussion.
